concern_details.detail: main components involved in seat booking and their responsibilities
concern_details.why: The booking path is correct: UIs -> REST -> LibraryFacade -> ReservationManager, plus AssignmentStrategy and StudyRoomManager. But the rule-bearing logic is spread over classes that the view merges into one 'Reservation domain model' box: StudyRoom.isActive/isOpenOnDate/getScheduledTimeSlots, Seat.isAvailable, Area.getAvailableSeats, Student.hasActiveOrConfirmedReservationForDateAndSlot, and the Reservation state classes. Because of the merge the developer cannot see which part holds which rule. Several boxes also have no responsibility text (LibraryFacade, NotificationManager, NotificationScheduler, Registries).

concern_details.detail: how they interact with each other
concern_details.why: Labelled caller->callee arrows show the main call chain. But AssignmentStrategy and NotificationService are interfaces in the code (pluggable strategy, adapter wired in NotificationConfiguration), and the view shows them only as plain arrows. The Observer link (Reservation.attach(NotificationManager), notifyObservers) is admitted in the README but not drawn: the arrow ReservationManager -> NotificationManager 'notifies student' hides that the notification goes through the Reservation subject. The room and slot queries the wizard makes before booking are also missing: web -> /api/rooms/available, timeslots and room detail on StudyRoomController, and Swing -> getAvailableStudyRooms/getAvailableTimeSlots. Only '/api/reservations' is drawn.

concern_details.detail: which parts of the system may be affected by the modification
concern_details.why: The blue/grey legend marks ReservationManager, AssignmentStrategy and the domain model as edit points. That is a reasonable start, but it is too coarse to act on. (a) The slot-occupancy rule ReservationRegistry.occupiesSlot (ACTIVE or CONFIRMED counts as occupied) lives in the Registries box, which is not marked. (b) StudyRoomManager.countAvailableSeats reuses Area.getAvailableSeats, so any availability rule changes the counts the UIs show. The view does not mark this ripple. (c) The rules are listed in a note, but the note does not say which class each rule lives in. (d) MakeReservationTest, the existing test of these rules, is not mentioned. (e) Whether ReservationRequestDTO and the UIs must change when a rule needs new input is not shown. Colour-only marking also relies on the legend instead of the model.

level_why: There are 14 elements; the README itself says this is over the 12-element budget. Several elements do nothing for a developer adding booking rules: NotificationScheduler (end-of-reservation and reminders, not booking), NotificationServiceAdapter, the MySQL database, and arguably PersistenceManager. Detail is spent on the periphery, while the one area where it matters, the domain model where rules actually live, is collapsed into a single box. Drop or merge the periphery (notification stack into one 'Notification' component, persistence and DB into one 'Persistence (JPA/MySQL)' or omit). Split the domain box into the rule-bearing parts: StudyRoom/TimeSlot (open, active, schedule), Seat/Area (availability), Student (uniqueness) and Reservation+states.
unsupported: ReservationManager -> NotificationManager 'notifies student' drawn as a direct call: the code (ReservationManager.notifyReservation, lines 107-110) attaches NotificationManager as an Observer of the Reservation and calls reservation.notifyObservers(). The dependency is real, but the interaction runs through the domain model's Observer interface.

NotificationManager -> NotificationServiceAdapter as a direct dependency: NotificationManager depends only on the NotificationService interface, and NotificationConfiguration injects NotificationServiceAdapter at startup. It should be a required/provided interface, not a direct arrow.

NotificationScheduler -> LibraryFacade 'ends, reminds' is supported (NotificationScheduler.java:23-29) but is not part of seat booking; drawing it inside a make-reservation view implies a role it does not have.

Grey legend calls NotificationScheduler 'probably unaffected', but manageReservationEnd moves reservations out of ACTIVE/CONFIRMED, which changes what occupiesSlot counts as occupied. Rules involving reservation lifetime or state would touch it, so the legend's claim is not safe.
missing: ReservationRegistry.occupiesSlot (ReservationRegistry.java:120-123): the rule defining which reservation states block a seat; a key edit point for new booking rules, hidden in the unmarked Registries box.

Where each existing rule lives: room active/open in ReservationManager.resolveRoom with StudyRoom.isActive/isOpenOnDate; slot timing in resolveTimeSlot with StudyRoom.getScheduledTimeSlots; uniqueness in Student.hasActiveOrConfirmedReservationForDateAndSlot; seat availability in Seat.isAvailable and Area.getAvailableSeats; seat-in-area check in validateSeatInArea. The merged domain box and the note leave this out.

The ripple from availability rules into StudyRoomManager.countAvailableSeats (StudyRoomManager.java:378-384) and the room, slot and seat-map queries used by both UIs. Those queries go through StudyRoomController /api/rooms/* (StudyRoomController.java:44-65) and Swing DateAndRoomSelection/TimeSlotSelection/SeatSelection, and the view draws neither path.
AssignmentStrategy as an interface with its realisation FirstAvailableAssignment (set in ReservationManager.getInstance), so the developer sees the extension point for seat-choice rules.

The ReservationRequestDTO contract between UIs/REST and ReservationManager. A new rule that needs new input must change it, together with ReservationController, ReservationSummary and reservation.html.
MakeReservationTest (src/test/.../MakeReservationTest.java) as an affected part when rules change.
uml: All relations are drawn as solid open arrows (PlantUML '-->'), which read as directed associations. Between components, use dependencies (dashed arrows, optionally «use») or assembly connectors between provided and required interfaces.

No interfaces are modelled, although the code has explicit ones on the booking path: AssignmentStrategy, NotificationService and Observer. A UML component diagram should show these as provided (lollipop) and required (socket) interfaces, especially AssignmentStrategy, which is the extension point for seat-assignment rules.

The MySQL database is drawn as a plain component. It is an external store; either place it outside the system boundary as an external component (UML has no standard «database» stereotype for components), or omit it. Do not present it as an application component.

Custom stereotypes <<accent>> and <<muted>> are attached to elements; they are hidden in the render, but in the model they are non-standard stereotypes used for styling. The 'affected' status should not rely on colour stereotypes. State it in the model, for example in a note naming the affected components, or with tagged text.
There is no system boundary (a subsystem or component enclosing the application), so external parts (browser pages, email gateway, DB) are not distinguished from internal components.
fixes: Split the 'Reservation domain model' box into the rule-bearing parts (StudyRoom/TimeSlot, Seat/Area, Student, Reservation+states). Attach to each a short note of the rules it holds and where (resolveRoom/isOpenOnDate, resolveTimeSlot, hasActiveOrConfirmedReservationForDateAndSlot, Seat.isAvailable/Area.getAvailableSeats). Also mark ReservationRegistry.occupiesSlot as an edit point.

Drop NotificationScheduler, NotificationServiceAdapter and the MySQL DB, and merge PersistenceManager into the Registries or a single persistence component. Keep at most one 'Notification' component, reached through the Observer interface.

Model the interfaces: AssignmentStrategy as an interface provided by FirstAvailableAssignment and required by ReservationManager, plus Observer and NotificationService if notification stays. Change all relations to dependency or assembly notation instead of solid associations.

Show the availability ripple: StudyRoomManager.countAvailableSeats -> Area.getAvailableSeats, and the UIs' room, slot and seat-map queries via StudyRoomController /api/rooms/* and the Swing wizard screens. Mark StudyRoomManager as affected by availability rules.

State the affected parts in the model rather than colour only. Include the ReservationRequestDTO and UI/REST contract as 'changes only if the rule needs new input', and name MakeReservationTest as needing updates.
